- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. content.text:
r01.

The premise is incorrect — there is no Redis connection in this repository. The cache layer is an **in-memory Go cache**, not Redis-backed.

The cache is implemented in `store/cache/cache.go` as a thread-safe in-memory store using `sync.Map` with TTL-based expiration. It is instantiated in `store/store.go:38-45`, where `Store.New()` creates a `cache.Config` with a **default TTL of 10 minutes** (`10 * time.Minute`) for all cache entries, including user entries. The `userCache` field (`store/store.go:28`) is created with this same config at `store/store.go:52`.

User entries are cached by user ID (key derived via `userCacheKey()` in `store/user.go:88-90`) using the default `Set()` method (`store/user.go:98, 122, 132, 143, 167`), which applies the default 10-minute TTL. There is no per-type TTL override for user entries — they use the same `DefaultTTL` as all other cached data. Expired entries are cleaned up by a background goroutine running every 5 minutes (`CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute` at `store/cache/cache.go:61`).
